answer:
You can use `promptfoo retry <evalId>` to re-run only the errored test cases from a specific eval. The docs describe it this way: "Retry all ERROR results from a specific eval. This command finds test cases that resulted in errors (e.g., from network issues, rate limits, or API failures) and re-runs only those test cases. The results are updated in place in the original eval." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

For example:

```sh
promptfoo retry eval-abc123
```

The docs list other options, such as `-c updated-config.yaml` for a different config file and `--max-concurrency 2` to limit concurrency. [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

If you want to retry the most recent eval instead, use `promptfoo eval --retry-errors`, which "retries all ERROR results from the latest eval" [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]. This flag "Cannot be used together with `--resume` or `--no-write` flags." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

If a retry fails, your original errors are kept: "Old ERROR results are only removed after the retry succeeds." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md] You can run the command again safely.
